title: Count Unreachable Pairs After Edge Removals
statement:
You are given an undirected, connected, acyclic graph (a tree) with `n` nodes numbered `0` to `n - 1` and `n - 1` edges `e1, e2, ..., e(n-1)`, listed in the order in which they will be removed.

The edges are removed one by one, and the removals accumulate: after removing `e1`, then after removing `e1` and `e2`, and so on. After the `i`-th removal, let `c_i` be the number of unordered pairs of nodes `(u, v)`, `u ≠ v`, that can no longer reach each other, i.e. that lie in different connected components of the graph formed by the edges `e(i+1), ..., e(n-1)` that are still present. Clearly `c_1 ≤ c_2 ≤ ...`.

Print the array `c_1, c_2, ..., c_(n-1)`. Its length equals the number of edges.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n - 1` lines contains two integers `u` and `v`: an edge between nodes `u` and `v` (0-indexed). The edges are given in removal order.
constraints: the given edges form a tree
answers can reach about 5 · 10^9, so use 64-bit integers

examples.explanation: After removing 0-1 the components are {0} and {1,2,3}: 3 unreachable pairs. After removing 1-2 as well they are {0}, {1}, {2,3}: 6 total pairs minus 1 connected pair = 5. After removing 2-3 every node is alone: 6.

A star with centre 0. Removing 0-1 isolates node 1 from the other 4 nodes: 4 pairs. After 0-2 the components are {0,3,4}, {1}, {2}: 10 - 3 = 7. After 0-3: {0,4}, {1}, {2}, {3}: 10 - 1 = 9. After 0-4 all are isolated: 10.

hints: After all edges are removed, every pair is unreachable: n(n-1)/2. Counting what happens when edges are removed in order is awkward, so think about the process backwards.
In reverse, start with no edges and add the edges from last to first. A union-find structure tracks the component sizes.
Merging two components of sizes a and b makes exactly a·b new pairs reachable. Keep a running count of reachable pairs and subtract it from n(n-1)/2 to get each c_i.
